title: d-11: generated-app-composition
description:
## Deliverables
1. Wire real generated service/storage/cron in daemon/CLI/schema/config/hooks/wizard for SQLite/Postgres/MySQL and supported combined layouts. SQLite app data and cron rows default to one app file and the same SqliteDatabase/channel writer; remove cron.db/database_path and SQLx SQLite driver — REQ-RUN-0328; ANC-021/028/032.
2. Reject db=none+cron=true before generation. Invoke d-9 migration only on an explicitly supplied legacy cron file, preserving existing rows; no ongoing second cron database — REQ-RUN-0326; ANC-029.
3. Exercise actual CLI/HTTP/MCP read/write paths with real Python/Monty transforms and live claimed engines; update generation/getting-started docs and generation tests with the shipped0.3.0 interfaces — REQ-RUN-0201/0302/0702; ADR-RUN-0021.



4. Invoke d-3's single manifest checker on the real generated outputs; Every registry requirement in the template manifests changed here is >= its tested floor with no upper bound (ANC-037); no second checker or policy fixture set. Final recommended Cargo.lock and .sc-runtime/ metadata generation/delivery are d-12-owned.

## This sprint does not close
Eight-crate publication and actual upstream beads-cache migration/registry-only proof are d-12. This sprint runs development-source generated consumers and may not call them registry proof. No synchronization/code generator/config reload/unspecified permissions feature.
design:
Consumes real d-6 SQLite, d-7/d-8 engine backends, d-9 domain adapter, d-10 command/transform code, d-4 generation tooling and d-3 manifest checker. Compose concrete stores for each selected layout; cloned handles share the one SQLite database/writer. Mixed-adaptor source trees are owned here. This sprint closes generated composition/lifecycle; d-12 independently prepares publication and recommendations, then merges this completed integration before uploading. No recommendation generator or repeated checker fixtures live here.
Existing cargo-generate layout names/file choices remain unchanged: no-db+cron rejection uses the owned wizard answers schema and existing post-generation validation hook. d-11 does not edit template/cargo-generate.toml; d-12 is its sole owner and applies release lock/post-hook changes only after merging completed d-11 composition.
acceptance_criteria:
req:REQ-RUN-0328/shared-storage — Live generated SQLite app+cron rows use the same database/handle, one writer owning its only write connection, per root writer constraints. Async callers await without blocking/spawn_blocking. cargo metadata/tree shows one patched libsqlite3-sys>=0.39 and no SQLx SQLite driver, for cron on/off and selected combined layouts; cargo deny check advisories clears target SQLite/rmcp advisories. Reader blocking_recv runs only on dedicated non-async worker threads with no runtime; async storage callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes (ANC-027). Other engines implement shared Storage<T> without SQLite exposure unless selected.
req:REQ-CRON-0004/app-db — Preserve one active schedule per name, caller-supplied row limits including unlimited, stable IDs and per-row (id,generation) FENCED rejection; atomic set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled remain all-or-nothing. Port actual two-process assertions with controlled process/channel barriers; preserve source crosswalk semantics. Populated cron.db migration retains every schedule field in app DB and reruns safely.
req:REQ-RUN-0326/layouts — db=none+cron rejected before any generated output; supported layouts render/build and actual cron uses app storage, no cron.db default setting.
req:REQ-RUN-0201/transforms — Actual CLI/HTTP/MCP service read/write runs the real Python/Monty transform; failures retain typed errors. Live SQLite/Postgres/MySQL services and selected combined layouts execute actual end-to-end procedures; no doubles stand in for engine/transport proof.
Required: just lint; just test; cargo build --workspace; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml; full generation unittest suite, tests/integration/storage-v2 live engine/transport procedures and target advisory checks on fresh generated resolves. Docs/links match actual generated APIs. No publication proof claimed.
Run the ONE shared async CronStorage conformance suite on actual generic SQLite/Postgres/MySQL providers through sc-cron CronStore; deterministic two-process providers port active-name/limit/fencing/atomic cases. Backends contain no CronRow type/schema/SQL. Legacy migration is d-9 app-owned code invoked by composition. Public storage failure/panic tests use typed Result semantics and real waiting callers, not a delay heuristic.
Full generated sqlite-postgres and sqlite-mysql layouts MUST resolve, build and execute with direct SQLx core/engine/macros dependencies selecting no SQLite feature, so no sqlx SQLite driver is in any graph, plus the patched rusqlite backend; current umbrella sets are known incompatible. Live query!/offline/migration behavior must pass, not inferred from lead cargo-check probe. Use cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys (one selected>=0.39) and -i sqlx-sqlite (no selected package), never Cargo.lock. Existing CLI/daemon/schema/api-types tests are this sprint's owned regressions. Actual sc-lint#931 no-panic and transaction-body analyzer checks apply to changed template storage code; until delivered and passing, closure remains blocked. Record their actual commands and external state when available; runtime tests never substitute for static analysis.
req:REQ-RUN-0328/mixed-dependencies — Direct sqlx-core/engine/macros requirements select NO SQLite feature; cargo tree -i sqlx-sqlite selects no package in sqlite-postgres/sqlite-mysql too. Generated/production crates gain no sc-compose or ATM dependency, enforced by existing boundary lint (ANC-012/028).
req:REQ-CRON-0004/limit — The live shared app database refuses new schedule rows at the embedding app's configured row limit; exercise the ported case against real providers (ANC-031). The conformance suite executes the generic atomic multi-row operation on SQLite, Postgres and MySQL, proving all-or-nothing behavior (ANC-033).
req:REQ-RUN-0328/selected-native-tree — The cargo tree of EVERY selected layout (SQLite alone, cron on/off, sqlite-postgres and sqlite-mysql) contains NO sqlx SQLite driver crate. SQLx direct core/driver/macros crates are selected only for Postgres/MySQL; cargo tree -i sqlx-sqlite must select nothing in every case (ANC-028).
req:REQ-RUN-0328/generator-compatibility — Generation/setup instructions declare the repository sc-compose CLI minimum as >=1.8.0, using .sc/generation-tools.json as the source. Run the supported layout generation procedures with CLI1.8.0 and compatible CLI commands; generation succeeds at that floor. d-4 owns that declared tool requirement and executable-selection check; d-11 updates the layout instructions and generation tests using it (ANC-003/005).
req:REQ-RUN-0328/lifecycle — Using controlled shutdown and writer-failure signals, stop HTTP/MCP intake and scheduler work, drain/cancel in-flight work under the existing grace budget, await SqliteDatabase::shutdown and join its writer before releasing runtime/logger ownership (ADR-RT-0005). Every admitted write commits or returns a typed failure; writer failure stops intake instead of leaving a healthy-looking daemon. Use existing runtime shutdown control, not a new health endpoint.
notes: Owns generated composition and live providers only. Actual upstream migration/publication belongs to d-12; obsolete coordination carve-out is retired.

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected eight public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 2 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract |
| d-11 | 3 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 3 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path3, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with only transaction name/mode properties. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Eight published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-storage first, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against eight published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
